title: I Enforced the Classroom Phone Basket on the Substitute Who Invented It

parts.text: I set my phone in the basket at 8:31 because the sub, Mr. Hale, said anyone who didn't would get detention. I was sixteen. He kept his own phone in his pocket and filmed the class for a "professional portfolio." He told us we had no expectation of privacy in public school. I asked if the basket was public. He said don't be smart. During independent work he answered a call on speaker about his real-estate closing. The kids in the front row heard the sale price. I wrote the time on a scrap of graph paper. Then he accused Maya of having a watch that texted, which it did not, and put her name on the detention list without the basket ever touching her desk.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He filmed us, took a closing call, and detentioned a kid whose watch did not text.

social.video_title: He made a phone basket and kept his in his pocket — Part 1/2
social.description: First period, a substitute filming a portfolio, and a speakerphone closing. Maya's watch was just a watch. Would you have spoken up?

parts.text: I told the assistant principal after the bell, with Maya, with the graph paper, with the district filming policy that required consent forms for portfolios. Hale's pocket phone had not gone in the basket. The detention list was voided. He did not come back. Our regular teacher returned Thursday and put the basket on the top shelf. We kept our phones away because she asked like a person. I still think about the sale price. It was a lot of house for a man who needed a basket to feel tall. Maya's watch kept time. That was all it had to do.

social.video_title: The portfolio had no consent forms — Part 2/2
social.description: District policy, a voided detention, and a basket that went on a shelf. Was speakerphone a lesson plan?
